tasks.title: Implement NextAuth.js Authentication System
tasks.description: Integrate NextAuth.js to manage user authentication. This includes setting up API routes for auth handling, middleware for protecting routes, and session management on the client-side.
tasks.details: Install the `next-auth` package using npm or yarn. Create a dynamic API route at `pages/api/auth/[...nextauth].js` to handle all authentication requests. Inside this file, configure the `NextAuth` options, including at least one authentication provider (e.g., Google, GitHub, or Credentials). Generate a `NEXTAUTH_SECRET` using `openssl rand -base64 32` and add it, along with `NEXTAUTH_URL` and any provider-specific client IDs and secrets, to the `.env.local` file. Wrap the main application component in `_app.js` with the `<SessionProvider>` to make session data globally available. Create a `middleware.js` file in the project root to define protected routes, which will automatically redirect unauthenticated users. For COPPA compliance, ensure the chosen authentication providers and data handling processes align with requirements for users under 13, or plan for an age-gating mechanism.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify that all required environment variables (`NEXTAUTH_SECRET`, `NEXTAUTH_URL`, provider keys) are present in `.env.local`. Attempt to navigate to a protected route and confirm you are redirected to the sign-in page. Complete the sign-in process with a configured provider. After a successful login, confirm you are redirected to the originally requested protected route. Use the `useSession` hook on a client page to display authenticated user data (e.g., name, email) and verify it is correct. Test the sign-out functionality to ensure the session is destroyed and the user is redirected appropriately. Check the browser's developer tools to confirm session cookies are created on login and deleted on logout.

subtasks.title: Install NextAuth.js and Configure Environment Variables
subtasks.description: Set up the foundational elements for NextAuth.js by installing the necessary package and configuring the required environment variables for security and functionality.
subtasks.details: Install the `next-auth` package using `npm install next-auth`. Generate a `NEXTAUTH_SECRET` using the command `openssl rand -base64 32`. Create a `.env.local` file in the project root. Add `NEXTAUTH_SECRET`, `NEXTAUTH_URL` (e.g., `http://localhost:3000` for development), and any provider-specific client IDs and secrets to this file.
subtasks.testStrategy: Verify that the `next-auth` package is added to `package.json`. Check that the `.env.local` file is created, populated, and ignored by version control. The application should start without errors related to missing NextAuth environment variables.

subtasks.title: Implement Backend Authentication API Route
subtasks.description: Implement the dynamic API route that NextAuth.js uses to handle all authentication-related server-side logic, including sign-in, sign-out, and session management.
subtasks.details: Create a new file at `pages/api/auth/[...nextauth].js`. Import `NextAuth` from `next-auth` and at least one authentication provider (e.g., `GoogleProvider` from `next-auth/providers/google`). Export a default function calling `NextAuth` with a configuration object that includes the `providers` array and the `secret` from `process.env.NEXTAUTH_SECRET`.
subtasks.testStrategy: Navigate to the default sign-in page at `/api/auth/signin`. The page should render correctly and display the configured authentication provider(s) as sign-in options. Check the server terminal for any configuration errors.

subtasks.title: Integrate SessionProvider for Global Client-Side State
subtasks.description: Wrap the root application component with the `SessionProvider` to make the user's authentication session data available throughout the client-side of the application via the `useSession` hook.
subtasks.details: Open the `pages/_app.js` (or `pages/_app.tsx`) file. Import `SessionProvider` from `next-auth/react`. Wrap the main `<Component {...pageProps} />` with `<SessionProvider session={pageProps.session}>`. This context provider will manage session state, refetching it periodically to keep it in sync.
subtasks.testStrategy: After signing in through the API route, use the `useSession` hook in a sample page component. Verify that the `data` object from `useSession` contains the user's information and the `status` is 'authenticated'.

subtasks.title: Implement Route Protection with Middleware
subtasks.description: Create a middleware file to protect specific pages or entire sections of the application, ensuring that only authenticated users can access them.
subtasks.details: Create a `middleware.js` (or `middleware.ts`) file in the project's root directory. Import `withAuth` from `next-auth/middleware`. Define and export a `config` object specifying the routes to protect using a `matcher` array (e.g., `matcher: ['/dashboard/:path*']`). Export the `withAuth` function as the default export.
subtasks.testStrategy: Attempt to access a protected route (e.g., `/dashboard`) while not logged in. Verify that you are redirected to the sign-in page. After logging in, verify that you can successfully access the protected route.

tasks.title: Migrate Backend Database from SQLite to PostgreSQL
tasks.description: Transition the application's backend database from SQLite to a production-ready PostgreSQL instance. This involves updating the data access layer, implementing connection pooling, and creating robust migration scripts.
tasks.details: 1. **Dependency Management:** Add the GORM PostgreSQL driver (`gorm.io/driver/postgres`) to the project's dependencies and remove the SQLite driver (`gorm.io/driver/sqlite`). 2. **Configuration:** Update the database initialization logic to construct the connection string from environment variables (e.g., `DB_HOST`, `DB_USER`, `DB_PASSWORD`, `DB_NAME`, `DB_PORT`, `DB_SSLMODE`). Do not hardcode credentials. 3. **Connection Logic:** Replace the GORM `sqlite.Open()` call with `postgres.Open()`. Configure the underlying `sql.DB` object for production use by setting up connection pooling (e.g., `SetMaxIdleConns`, `SetMaxOpenConns`, `SetConnMaxLifetime`). 4. **Database Migrations:** Implement or update the GORM `AutoMigrate` function to handle the creation and evolution of the database schema in PostgreSQL. Ensure all models, including those for users and sessions from the authentication system, are included in the migration. 5. **Local Development:** Update or create a `docker-compose.yml` file to include a PostgreSQL service for a consistent local development environment.
tasks.testStrategy: 1. **Connection Test:** On application startup, verify that the service successfully connects to the PostgreSQL database by checking application logs for connection success messages. Test that the application fails gracefully if connection variables are incorrect. 2. **Migration Verification:** Run the application and trigger the migration. Connect to the PostgreSQL database using a client (e.g., `psql`, DBeaver) and inspect the schema. Confirm that all expected tables, columns, and constraints have been created correctly. 3. **CRUD Functionality:** Manually test or run integration tests for all existing API endpoints that perform database operations (Create, Read, Update, Delete) to ensure they function as expected against the PostgreSQL database. 4. **Authentication Flow:** Test the full user registration and login flow to ensure user and session data is correctly persisted and retrieved from the new PostgreSQL database.

tasks.title: Implement Advanced User Profile and Compliance Models
tasks.description: Create comprehensive user-related data models including LearningProfile, DiagnosticResult, and AccessibilityPreferences. This task also involves implementing data structures for COPPA compliance, parental consent, and enhanced support for neurodivergent learners.
tasks.details: Extend the base user model provided by NextAuth.js by creating and associating several new data models in the PostgreSQL database. 1. **LearningProfile Model**: Create a table to store individual learning preferences. Fields should include `userId` (foreign key), `learningStyle` (e.g., 'visual', 'auditory', 'kinesthetic'), `preferredPace` ('slow', 'medium', 'fast'), and a JSONB field for `subjectStrengthsWeaknesses`. 2. **DiagnosticResult Model**: Create a table to log results from assessments. Fields should include `userId` (foreign key), `assessmentId`, `score`, `completedAt` (timestamp), and a JSONB field `detailedResults` to store granular response data. 3. **AccessibilityPreferences Model**: Create a table for user-specific accessibility settings. Fields should include `userId` (foreign key), `fontSize` (number), `contrastMode` ('default', 'high'), `enableTextToSpeech` (boolean), and `prefersReducedMotion` (boolean). 4. **COPPA Compliance**: Modify the core `User` model to include a `dateOfBirth` field. Implement a `ParentalConsent` model with fields like `childUserId` (foreign key), `parentEmail`, `consentStatus` ('pending', 'granted', 'revoked'), `requestDate`, and `consentDate`. Business logic must be added during user registration to check age based on `dateOfBirth` and trigger the parental consent workflow if the user is a minor (e.g., under 13). All models should be defined using the project's ORM and a new database migration script must be created to apply these schema changes to the PostgreSQL database.
tasks.testStrategy: 1. **Migration Verification**: Run the migration script against a test database. Use a database client to inspect the schema and confirm that all new tables (`LearningProfiles`, `DiagnosticResults`, `AccessibilityPreferences`, `ParentalConsents`) and the new fields on the `Users` table are created correctly with the specified columns, types, and foreign key constraints. 2. **Model CRUD Operations**: Write unit tests for the data access layer to verify Create, Read, Update, and Delete operations for each new model. Ensure that creating a user and then creating an associated `LearningProfile` works as expected. 3. **COPPA Logic Testing**: Create a test case for user registration where the `dateOfBirth` makes the user a minor. Verify that a `ParentalConsent` record is automatically created with a 'pending' status. Create another test case for an adult user and verify no `ParentalConsent` record is created. 4. **API Endpoint Simulation**: Test the API endpoints (once created) for updating accessibility preferences and ensure the changes are correctly persisted and can be retrieved for the user. Verify that a user can only access their own related data.

subtasks.title: Extend User Model and Create AccessibilityPreferences Model
subtasks.description: Modify the core `User` model to include a `dateOfBirth` field for age verification. Concurrently, define and create the `AccessibilityPreferences` model to store user-specific accessibility settings.
subtasks.details: Using the project's ORM (e.g., Prisma), add a `dateOfBirth: DateTime` field to the `User` model. Create a new model `AccessibilityPreferences` with fields: `id`, `userId` (one-to-one relation to User), `fontSize` (Int), `contrastMode` (Enum: 'DEFAULT', 'HIGH'), `enableTextToSpeech` (Boolean), and `prefersReducedMotion` (Boolean). Ensure the relation between `User` and `AccessibilityPreferences` is correctly defined.
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit test the model definitions to ensure correct types and relations. Verify that a `User` can be created with a `dateOfBirth` and that an `AccessibilityPreferences` record can be created and associated with a user.

subtasks.title: Implement the LearningProfile Model
subtasks.description: Define and create the `LearningProfile` model to store individual learning preferences and styles for each user.
subtasks.details: In the ORM schema, create a new `LearningProfile` model. It should have a one-to-one relationship with the `User` model via a `userId` foreign key. Include the following fields: `learningStyle` (Enum: 'VISUAL', 'AUDITORY', 'KINESTHETIC'), `preferredPace` (Enum: 'SLOW', 'MEDIUM', 'FAST'), and `subjectStrengthsWeaknesses` (JSONB). This JSONB field will store unstructured data about subject-specific performance.
subtasks.testStrategy: Write unit tests to validate the creation and updating of `LearningProfile` records. Test the correct storage and retrieval of data from the `subjectStrengthsWeaknesses` JSONB field.

subtasks.title: Implement the DiagnosticResult Model
subtasks.description: Define and create the `DiagnosticResult` model to log the outcomes of user assessments and diagnostic tests.
subtasks.details: Using the ORM, create a new `DiagnosticResult` model. It should have a many-to-one relationship with the `User` model (a user can have many results). Fields should include: `id`, `userId` (foreign key), `assessmentId` (String), `score` (Float), `completedAt` (DateTime), and `detailedResults` (JSONB). The `detailedResults` field will store granular data like question-by-question answers.
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit test the model to ensure a `DiagnosticResult` can be created and linked to a `User`. Test serialization and deserialization of the `detailedResults` JSONB field.

subtasks.title: Implement the ParentalConsent Model for COPPA Compliance
subtasks.description: Define and create the `ParentalConsent` model to manage the parental consent process for users who are minors, as required by COPPA.
subtasks.details: Create a new `ParentalConsent` model in the ORM. It should have a one-to-one relationship with the `User` model, referencing the child's user ID (`childUserId`). The model must include the fields: `parentEmail` (String), `consentStatus` (Enum: 'PENDING', 'GRANTED', 'REVOKED'), `requestDate` (DateTime), and `consentDate` (DateTime, nullable).
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit test the `ParentalConsent` model. Verify that records can be created with a 'PENDING' status and later updated to 'GRANTED' or 'REVOKED'. Ensure the relationship to the child's `User` account is correctly established.

subtasks.title: Generate Database Migration and Implement COPPA Registration Logic
subtasks.description: Generate a consolidated database migration script to apply all new model schemas to the PostgreSQL database. Implement the business logic within the user registration flow to check the user's age and trigger the parental consent workflow if they are under 13.
subtasks.details: Run the ORM's migration command (e.g., `prisma migrate dev --name add-user-profile-models`) to generate a single SQL migration file. Review the generated script to ensure it correctly creates all new tables and alters the `User` table. In the user registration service/API endpoint, add logic that calculates the user's age from the provided `dateOfBirth`. If the age is under 13, prevent full account activation and instead create a `ParentalConsent` record with a 'PENDING' status.
subtasks.testStrategy: Integration test the user registration endpoint. Test three scenarios: 1) User over 13 registers successfully. 2) User under 13 attempts to register, resulting in a `ParentalConsent` record being created. 3) Registration with an invalid date of birth fails gracefully. Manually apply the migration to a test database and verify the schema using a DB client.

tasks.title: Setup MCP Server for AI Diagnostic Tools
tasks.description: Establish the Model Context Protocol (MCP) server infrastructure using PydanticAI. This involves creating MCP resources for ADHD and dyslexia diagnostic assessments and configuring a client for external tool integration.
tasks.details: 1. **Install Dependencies**: Add `pydantic-ai` to the project's dependencies. 2. **Create Diagnostic Resources**: Implement two new classes, `ADHD_Assessment` and `Dyslexia_Assessment`, that inherit from `pydantic_ai.mcp.MCP_Resource`. Each class will encapsulate the logic for its respective diagnostic tool. The primary method (e.g., `run_assessment`) in each class will take user-specific context and return a structured result, ideally mapping to the `DiagnosticResult` model from Task 3. 3. **Implement MCP Server**: Create a new service or script to instantiate and run an `pydantic_ai.mcp.MCP_Server`. Register the `ADHD_Assessment` and `Dyslexia_Assessment` resources with the server instance. This server will expose the registered resources over a network protocol (e.g., HTTP/S). 4. **Database Integration**: Within the resource methods, implement logic to connect to the PostgreSQL database (setup in Task 2) and persist the outcomes of the assessments. This involves creating and saving `DiagnosticResult` records (defined in Task 3) linked to the authenticated user's ID (from Task 1). 5. **Client Configuration**: Develop a simple client-side module using `pydantic_ai.mcp.MCP_Client` to demonstrate connectivity. This client should be able to connect to the server, list available resources, and invoke a diagnostic method, proving the integration path for external tools.
tasks.testStrategy: 1. **Unit Tests**: Create unit tests for the `ADHD_Assessment` and `Dyslexia_Assessment` resource classes in isolation. Mock database connections and AI model responses to verify the internal logic and data transformation. 2. **Server Initialization Test**: Write a test to ensure the MCP server starts correctly, loads the configured resources, and binds to the specified port without errors. 3. **Client-Server Integration Test**: In an integration test, start the MCP server. Use the `MCP_Client` to connect to it, fetch the list of available resources, and confirm both `ADHD_Assessment` and `Dyslexia_Assessment` are present. 4. **End-to-End Test**: Execute a full diagnostic flow via the client. Invoke the `run_assessment` method on a resource, pass mock user data, and then query the test database to verify that a corresponding `DiagnosticResult` record was created accurately and associated with the correct test user.

tasks.title: Enhance AIDA Agent with Advanced PydanticAI Diagnostics
tasks.description: Upgrade the AIDA diagnostic agent by integrating advanced PydanticAI features for multi-modal assessment. This includes implementing evidence-based algorithms for ADHD/dyslexia screening, behavioral pattern recognition, and analysis of cognitive task performance.
tasks.details: Extend the `ADHD_Assessment` and `Dyslexia_Assessment` MCP resources created in Task 4. First, modify the input schemas to handle multi-modal data, using Pydantic models to define structured inputs for cognitive task results (e.g., reaction times, accuracy) and behavioral observations. Second, implement evidence-based screening algorithms by translating the logic from validated psychometric frameworks (e.g., concepts from ASRS, CTOPP-2) into Python functions within the assessment classes. These functions will process the multi-modal inputs to generate scores. Third, enhance the output to map directly to the `DiagnosticResult` model from Task 3, ensuring it includes confidence levels, sub-scale scores, and an AI-generated narrative summary. Leverage PydanticAI's structured output capabilities to enforce this schema reliably.
tasks.testStrategy: 1. **Algorithm Unit Tests**: Create unit tests for the new screening algorithms using mock data representing clear positive, negative, and borderline cases for both ADHD and dyslexia to validate the scoring logic. 2. **Multi-modal Input Validation**: Write tests to confirm that the Pydantic input models correctly parse and validate complex, multi-modal assessment data, including handling of malformed or incomplete inputs. 3. **End-to-End Integration Test**: Develop an integration test that sends a complete assessment request (with cognitive and behavioral data) to the MCP server endpoint. Verify that the enhanced AIDA agent processes the request and returns a well-formed `DiagnosticResult` object that matches the expected structure. 4. **Database Persistence Verification**: After a successful integration test, query the PostgreSQL database to ensure the generated `DiagnosticResult` is correctly saved and linked to the appropriate user ID.

tasks.title: Implement Accessibility-First Frontend Design System
tasks.description: Develop a comprehensive, accessibility-first frontend design system compliant with WCAG 2.2 AA. This system will include neurodivergent-specific UI components, customizable sensory settings, and support for multi-modal interactions.
tasks.details: 1. **Foundation & Tooling**: Establish a base using a headless UI library like Radix UI or Headless UI to ensure a solid, accessible foundation. Integrate with Tailwind CSS for styling. Set up Storybook to develop, document, and test components in isolation. 2. **WCAG 2.2 AA Compliance**: Systematically ensure all components meet WCAG 2.2 AA standards. This includes maintaining a minimum 4.5:1 color contrast ratio for text, creating highly visible focus states for all interactive elements, using semantic HTML, and applying appropriate ARIA attributes. 3. **Customizable Sensory Settings**: Implement a global ThemeProvider connected to the `AccessibilityPreferences` model (from Task 3). This provider will manage user-selected themes (e.g., high-contrast, dark mode, pastel), font sizes, and animation levels (e.g., 'full' vs 'reduced-motion'). Create API endpoints to persist these settings. 4. **Neurodivergent-Friendly Components**: Design UI components with clear, literal iconography and explicit labels. Develop a 'focus mode' component that simplifies the UI, hiding non-essential elements to reduce cognitive load. 5. **Multi-Modal Interaction**: Ensure complete keyboard navigability with a logical tab order. Test rigorously with screen readers (NVDA, VoiceOver). Implement an initial version of Voice User Interface (VUI) support using the Web Speech API for core navigation commands like 'go to dashboard' or 'open settings'.
tasks.testStrategy: 1. **Automated Accessibility Audits**: Integrate `axe-core` into the CI/CD pipeline and Storybook environment to automatically flag WCAG violations on every commit. 2. **Manual Keyboard Navigation Test**: Create a test plan that requires navigating through every interactive element of the application using only the keyboard (Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space). Verify logical focus order and full operability. 3. **Screen Reader Verification**: Perform end-to-end testing on key user flows using both NVDA and VoiceOver. Confirm that all content, form fields, and interactive elements are announced clearly and accurately. 4. **Preference Persistence Test**: As a test user, modify accessibility settings (e.g., change color theme, disable animations). Refresh the page, log out and back in, and verify that the chosen settings are correctly applied from the user's profile. 5. **VUI Command Test**: Execute a predefined list of voice commands and verify that the application correctly interprets them and performs the corresponding actions.

Set up a Storybook instance to develop, document, and test components in an isolated environment. Establish a clear directory structure for components, themes, and utilities.

Define a default color palette where text/background combinations meet a minimum 4.5:1 contrast ratio. Apply necessary ARIA attributes (e.g., `aria-label`, `aria-pressed`) as guided by Radix UI primitives and WAI-ARIA patterns. Document accessibility features for each component in Storybook.

subtasks.title: Implement Global ThemeProvider for Customizable Sensory Settings
subtasks.description: Create a global context provider (`ThemeProvider`) to manage and apply user-selected visual preferences across the entire application, connecting it to the `AccessibilityPreferences` model for persistence.
subtasks.details: Develop a React Context provider that manages the application's theme. This provider will expose functions to change themes (e.g., 'default', 'dark', 'high-contrast'), adjust the base font size, and toggle motion settings. The motion setting should respect the `prefers-reduced-motion` media query by default but allow user override. Refactor the core components from subtask 8 to consume styles (e.g., colors, fonts) from this provider. Create API hooks to fetch and save these settings via the backend.

subtasks.title: Develop Neurodivergent-Friendly Components and 'Focus Mode'
subtasks.description: Create specialized components and features designed to reduce cognitive load and enhance clarity for neurodivergent users, including a 'focus mode' to simplify the UI.
subtasks.details: Design and implement a set of icons that are literal and unambiguous, always paired with explicit text labels. Develop a 'Focus Mode' feature, which can be toggled by the user. When active, this mode should apply global CSS to hide or dim non-essential UI elements like decorative images, secondary navigation, and social media widgets, leaving only the primary task-related content and controls visible.

Write unit tests to verify that activating focus mode correctly applies the intended CSS classes or styles to the main application container. Conduct informal user feedback sessions on the clarity of icons and labels.

subtasks.description: Ensure the entire component library is fully operable via keyboard and screen readers. Additionally, implement a proof-of-concept Voice User Interface (VUI) for core navigation.

tasks.title: Implement User Profile and Accessibility Settings UI
tasks.description: Create the frontend interface and corresponding API endpoints for users to view and manage their personal learning profile and accessibility preferences. This will connect the backend user models to the frontend design system.
tasks.details: 1. **API Endpoint Creation**: In the Next.js application, create new API routes under `/api/user/`. Create a `profile.js` and `accessibility.js` file. The `GET` method on these routes should fetch the current logged-in user's `LearningProfile` and `AccessibilityPreferences` data from the database, using the session from NextAuth.js to identify the user. The `PUT` method should accept updated data, validate it, and save the changes. Ensure only the authenticated user can modify their own data. 2. **Frontend Page Implementation**: Create a new protected route, such as `/dashboard/settings`. This page will house the forms for updating user settings. Use a client-side data fetching library like SWR or React Query to call the API endpoints. 3. **UI Component Integration**: Build the settings forms using components from the accessibility-first design system (Task 6). Use `Select` components for `learningStyle`, `Toggle` or `Switch` components for boolean accessibility settings, and appropriate inputs for other fields. Manage form state and validation using a library like React Hook Form. 4. **State Management and Feedback**: On form submission, send the updated data to the `PUT` API endpoints. Provide clear user feedback, such as a toast notification for success and inline error messages for validation failures.
tasks.testStrategy: 1. **API Endpoint Verification**: Use an API client like Postman or write integration tests. Verify that `GET` requests to `/api/user/profile` and `/api/user/accessibility` return the correct data for an authenticated user and a 401 error for an unauthenticated one. Test the `PUT` endpoints with valid data, confirm the database is updated, and then test with invalid data to ensure a 400 error is returned. 2. **UI Functional Testing**: As a logged-in user, navigate to the settings page and verify that form fields are pre-populated with the correct data. Modify several settings, submit the form, and confirm a success message appears. Reload the page and verify the new settings have persisted. 3. **Access Control Test**: Attempt to access the `/dashboard/settings` page while logged out and confirm you are redirected to the login page. 4. **Accessibility Audit**: Run an `axe-core` scan on the settings page to ensure there are no accessibility violations and manually verify full keyboard navigability of the forms.

subtasks.details: In the Next.js application, create a new API route file at `/pages/api/user/profile.js`. Implement a `GET` handler that uses the NextAuth.js session to identify the logged-in user and fetches their `LearningProfile` from the database. Implement a `GET` handler to retrieve the `AccessibilityPreferences` for the authenticated user via their NextAuth.js session. subtasks.description: Perform targeted manual testing to ensure the application is fully usable by individuals relying on assistive technologies and to verify that all COPPA compliance logic is implemented correctly.
subtasks.details:
Create and execute a manual testing protocol for critical user flows using screen readers (NVDA and VoiceOver) and keyboard-only navigation to identify usability issues not caught by automated scans. Separately, develop and run a specific test plan to validate the entire COPPA parental consent workflow, including age-gating, consent request emails, and consent revocation, covering all edge cases.

subtasks.details:
Recruit a diverse group of testers, ensuring representation from neurodivergent communities. Develop detailed UAT scripts that guide participants through core application features like registration, taking a diagnostic, customizing their profile, and interacting with the dashboard. Establish a formal process for collecting, triaging, and prioritizing feedback using a dedicated tool or form.
